extracted.intended_audience: USPTO financial managers, auditors, oversight bodies (OMB/Congress), and external stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Policies, disclosure requirements, and audit-related standards used to prepare and evaluate the USPTO FY2021 financial statements, including accounting treatments, fund-restriction rules, program cost allocation, budgetary resource rules, contingency reporting, and auditor responsibilities. Focused on federal agency (USPTO) financial statement presentation and required supplementary disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: FECA actuarial liability calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The FECA actuarial liability is calculated annually, as of September 30th by the DOL. Projected annual payments were discounted to the present value based on averaging the Treasury’s Yield Curve for Treasury Nominal Coupon (TNC) issues for the current and prior four years to reflect the average duration in years for income and medical payments, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest rate assumptions utilized for discounting are disclosed (examples: 2021 — wage benefits: 2.23% in year 1; medical benefits: 2.06% in year 1; 2020 respective first-year rates provided). The report discloses the resulting estimated liability amounts ($9,666 thousand for 2021; $10,343 thousand for 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating lease disclosure and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating lease agreements for the USPTO’s office buildings are cancelable with appropriate notification and expire at various dates between FY 2022 and FY 2035. The GSA negotiates long-term office space leases and levies rent charges paid by the USPTO approximate to commercial rental rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report future minimum lease payments by fiscal year and disclose primary lease locations, initiation and expiration years. Provide total future minimum lease payments and explain relation to headquarters/regional office operating leases; disclose amounts paid to GSA for rent for the reporting years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments and contingencies reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is a party to various routine administrative proceedings, legal actions, and claims. Management discloses amounts that are reasonably possible and amounts where an adverse outcome is probable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimates where reasonably possible (example: ~$900 thousand reasonably possible for labor relations claims in 2021 vs ~$600 thousand in 2020) and disclose probable adverse outcome claim amounts (e.g., $415 thousand in 2021; $300 thousand in 2020). State whether payments were made from the Judgment Fund and whether there are major long-term commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment benefits disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-employment benefit expenses are disclosed by plan/category (CSRS, FERS, FEHB, FEGLI, FICA) and separated into funded and imputed components, with totals presented for each fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a table of funded vs imputed amounts and total cost for the year; include detail sufficient to show trends and any unusual items (e.g., negative amounts, unusual imputed financing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds from dedicated collections — definition and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds from dedicated collections are financed by specifically identified revenues, which remain available over time and are required by statute to be used for designated activities, benefits, or purposes, and must be accounted for separately from the government’s general revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose which funds qualify (e.g., Salaries and Expenses Fund, Fee Reserve Fund, Surcharge Fund), statutory basis (e.g., Leahy-Smith America Invents Act modifying 35 U.S.C. §42(c); OBRA 1990), balances in each fund, permitted uses, and any limitations (e.g., amounts available only as appropriated by Congress or subject to Treasury warrant). Note deposits/withholdings and any expirations or lack of Congressional reauthorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund rules (AIA / 35 U.S.C. §42(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund was created by the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act (Pub. L. No. 112-29) modifying 35 U.S.C §42(c), allowing the USPTO to collect and deposit fees collected in excess of appropriated levels into this fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose annual deposit activity (e.g., no deposit in 2021; $231,883 thousand deposited as of 9/30/2020), rules on availability (available without fiscal limitation until expended but subject to Congressional reprogramming requirements and appropriations), and subsequent Congressional approvals to spend deposited amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program cost classification and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Program costs consist of both costs related directly to the strategic goals and overall support costs allocated to the strategic goals. All costs are assigned to specific programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present program costs by cost category (personnel services and benefits; travel; rent; contractual services; etc.), separate direct and allocated costs, and show allocations (e.g., automation, resource management). Provide program-level presentations by strategic goal (Patent, Trademark, Intellectual Property Protection) with subtotals and totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of program costs by strategic goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Program costs are reported in columns corresponding to Strategic Goal 1 (Patent), Strategic Goal 2 (Trademark), and Strategic Goal 3 (Intellectual Property Protection), with direct costs by cost category and subtotaled before allocated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed cost line items per strategic goal and disclose the method of allocation for indirect/support costs so users can reconcile totals to the Statement of Net Cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary resources and carryover rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Total budgetary resources are primarily comprised of Congressional authority to spend current year fee collections. The USPTO receives an apportionment of Category A funds from OMB. Carryover (operating reserve) is derived from year-end budgetary resources that have not been obligated and usage of fees in the following fiscal year is on a first-in, first-out basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose appropriated amounts, under-/over-collections (e.g., FY2021 collected $96,340 thousand less than appropriated), carryover amounts brought into the fiscal year (e.g., $744,641 thousand into FY2021 with breakdown), and explain apportionment category and any Category B absence. Quantify reimbursable obligations and any significant variances vs appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding limitations and statutory restrictions on fee use
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act (35 U.S.C. §42(c)), fees available under relevant statutes may be used only for processing patents/trademarks and related activities and to cover a proportionate share of administrative costs. Some collections may be temporarily unavailable pursuant to Public Law and certain funds may be sequestered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose amounts temporarily unavailable (e.g., $1,171,348 thousand as of 9/30/2021), any statutory withholdings (e.g., $233,529 thousand withheld per OBRA 1990), sequestration amounts (e.g., $147,733 thousand sequestered pursuant to Pub. L. No. 113-6), and the legal citation for restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undelivered orders reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose reimbursable undelivered orders by intragovernmental and with-the-public components, showing unpaid and paid amounts and totals as of the reporting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables showing unpaid/paid totals and comparisons to prior year (e.g., FY2021 total undelivered orders intragovernmental $21,503 and with the public $513,525). Explain nature of obligations and relation to future delivery of goods/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary activities recognition and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiduciary activities are the collection/receipt and the management, protection, accounting, and disposition by the federal government of cash or other assets in which non-federal individuals or entities have an ownership interest that the federal government must uphold. Fiduciary cash and other assets are not assets of the federal government and accordingly are not recognized on the proprietary financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the legal basis for collections held in fiduciary capacity (e.g., Patent Cooperation Treaty, Madrid Protocol Implementation Act), schedule of fiduciary activity (contributions, disbursements, increases/decreases), and fiduciary net assets as of the reporting date, shown separately by program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation of Net Cost to Net Outlays methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconciliation explains the relationship between budgetary and proprietary accounting by listing key differences between net cost (accrual basis) and net outlays (budgetary basis). It identifies components of net cost that are not part of net outlays and components of net outlays that are not part of net cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a reconciliation table showing line items such as depreciation, changes in accounts receivable, changes in liabilities (accounts payable, federal employee benefits payable), imputed financing, acquisition of capital assets, transfers in without reimbursements, and compute net outlays. Disclose amounts by intragovernmental and with-the-public where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred maintenance and repairs (DM&R) policy and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred maintenance and repairs are maintenance and repairs that were not performed when they should have been, that were scheduled and not performed, or that were delayed for a future period. Maintenance and repairs exclude activities aimed at expanding capacity or upgrading an asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe PP&E categories covered, agency policy on DM&R (USPTO policy: DM&R do not arise for PP&E at the USPTO and no periodic assessment is performed), explain maintenance prioritization practices, user feedback meetings, and replacement cycles. If DM&R exist, agencies must disclose their prioritization and dollar amounts; USPTO explicitly states none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent auditor and management responsibilities and applicable audit standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Management is responsible for preparation and fair presentation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles; auditors' responsibility is to express an opinion in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States, Government Auditing Standards, and OMB Bulletin No. 21-04.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditor must plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether statements are free from material misstatement. The auditor's report should state whether financial statements are fairly presented, whether material weaknesses in internal control were identified, and whether there were reportable instances of noncompliance. The independent auditor (KPMG) opinion and scope statements are to be disclosed.
